name: Medial Collateral Ligament (MCL) Injury
summary: Valgus-related injury of the medial knee ligament complex, often managed non-operatively when isolated.

firstSteps: Protect from valgus stress and control swelling
Use brace/crutches if needed based on severity
Restore extension, flexion and quadriceps activation

tests.name: Valgus Stress Test at 30°
tests.purpose: Assess MCL laxity with reduced contribution from capsule and cruciate structures.
tests.positive: Medial pain and/or increased medial joint opening with altered endpoint.

stages.label: Protection, Education & Symptom-Guided Loading
stages.goal: Address safety, settle excessive irritability and maintain useful movement.
do: Protect from valgus stress and control swelling
Use brace/crutches if needed based on severity
Restore extension, flexion and quadriceps activation
dose: Quad sets: 3 x 10; heel slides 2–3 x 10
Weight bear as tolerated if stable and medically cleared
moveOn: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.

stages.label: Mobility, Strength & Capacity
stages.goal: Restore the specific strength, mobility and control required by the condition.
when: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.
moveOn: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.

stages.label: Functional Restoration & Return to Activity
stages.goal: Rebuild real-world, occupational or sporting capacity.
when: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.
do: Progress running, cutting and contact exposure
Use functional testing and stability assessment
Return based on grade, associated injury and sport demands
dose: Progress speed and contact exposure separately
moveOn: Full task exposure is completed progressively.
No clinically meaningful deterioration during the following 24 hours.

returnCriteria: No medial instability on clinical review
Strength, hop and cutting tasks appropriate to sport

structures: Possible medial meniscus and posteromedial corner involvement
classification: Grade III complete tear; assess associated instability
investigations: Radiographs when trauma/fracture criteria met; MRI if high-grade or associated injury suspected.
Orthopaedic referral for gross instability or multiligament injury.
manual: Maintain patellar/tibiofemoral mobility if restricted without stressing healing MCL.
Avoid valgus stress or aggressive medial soft-tissue techniques in acute phase.
modalities: Brace may protect higher-grade injury during early healing.
Ice/compression for comfort and swelling; exercise remains core.
mistakes: Testing valgus laxity aggressively in acute pain
Returning based only on pain reduction
pearls: Valgus laxity in full extension raises concern for broader capsuloligamentous injury.
Many isolated MCL injuries respond well to structured non-operative rehabilitation.

tests.name: Valgus Stress Test at 30°
tests.purpose: Assess MCL laxity with reduced contribution from capsule and cruciate structures.
tests.positive: Medial pain and/or increased medial joint opening with altered endpoint.
tests.patientPosition: Supine; stabilise thigh, apply controlled valgus force at knee with leg supported at 30° flexion.
tests.therapistPosition: Position yourself to observe and stabilise the relevant segment without forcing the movement.
tests.handPlacement: Use comfortable, controlled contact appropriate to the test; avoid painful compression or excessive force.
procedure: Explain the test and obtain consent.
Screen contraindications and compare sides when appropriate.
Perform the movement slowly and apply only the required resistance or stress.
Record familiar symptom reproduction, range, strength and side-to-side difference.
tests.interpretation: Compare with opposite side; laxity in full extension suggests more extensive injury.
tests.clinicalNote: A special test modifies clinical probability; it does not confirm a diagnosis in isolation.
